title: Major depression: episode, severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's depressive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for depression.

HPI
The patient is a 52-year-old man presenting today for a follow-up evaluation of his major depressive disorder, recurrent. He reports that his mood has been consistently low over the past several weeks. He describes a persistent lack of energy and a diminished interest in his usual hobbies. He notes that his sleep has been interrupted, often waking up in the early morning and having difficulty returning to sleep. He reports a noticeable decrease in concentration at work but denies any changes in appetite. He states that his current symptoms are moderate in intensity, impacting his daily functioning but not preventing him from completing his primary responsibilities. He is currently taking his prescribed medications as directed and reports no significant side effects.

Medication List
Sertraline 100mg daily

Review of Systems
Negative for chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. Negative for fevers or chills. Negative for weight changes. Denies any changes in vision or hearing. Denies any thoughts of self-harm. Negative for tremors or muscle weakness.

Social History
The patient is currently employed full-time in a management role. He lives with his wife and two children. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and enjoys watching movies on weekends. He denies any tobacco use.

Family History
Father has a history of hypertension. Mother has a history of type 2 diabetes. No known history of mental health conditions in the immediate family.

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 128/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Temperature: 98.6 F
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 98% on room air
Height: 5'10"
Weight: 195 lbs

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 5.7%
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
CMP: Within normal limits.

Exam
The patient is a well-groomed man who appears his stated age. He is cooperative and maintains good eye contact throughout the encounter. Speech is normal in rate and volume. Mood is reported as "down" and affect is congruent. Thought process is linear and goal-oriented. Cognition is intact. No acute physical distress noted.

Assessment
1. Major depressive disorder, recurrent. The patient is currently experiencing a moderate episode of depression.

Plan
1. Continue current dose of Sertraline 100mg daily.
2. Monitor for any changes in mood or side effects.
3. Patient advised to utilize coping strategies and maintain a regular sleep schedule.
4. Follow up in four weeks for continued monitoring of symptoms.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate (HCC 155): F33.1.

distractors.why: The provider documents moderate (HCC 155); mild has no HCC.
Severity is documented: do not use the unspecified code.
